title: Climate Change Impact on Water Resources (CCIWR)
description: A multi-model ensemble dataset of projected future changes in water resources (total runoff, diffuse groundwater recharge, and actual evapotranspiration) across all global land areas at 0.5° resolution, derived from the ISIMIP3b simulation archive by Earth Blox. The dataset spans 4 global hydrological models × 5 CMIP6 climate models × 3 emissions scenarios (SSP1-2.6, SSP3-7.0, SSP5-8.5) across three 30-year future horizons centred on 2030, 2055, and 2085, enabling uncertainty-aware analysis of climate change impacts on hydrology.

## README.md
# Climate Change Impact on Water Resources (CCIWR)

A multi-model ensemble dataset of projected future changes in water resources across all global land areas, from [Earth Blox](https://earthblox.io).

<!-- Accompanying blog post: <placeholder link> -->

## General description

Climate projections of water availability are inherently uncertain: different global
hydrological models (GHMs) respond differently to the same climate forcing, and different
global climate models (GCMs) produce different forcings for the same emission scenario.
Working with a **multi-model ensemble** — rather than a single model run — is therefore
essential to characterise this uncertainty honestly and to support risk-aware adaptation
decisions. By spanning 4 GHMs × 5 GCMs × 3 SSPs, the dataset exposed here samples the
main axes of uncertainty and allows users to derive robust statistics (medians, percentiles,
model agreement) rather than relying on a potentially unrepresentative single trajectory.

This document describes the structure of the derived Zarr store built from that archive
and provides ready-to-run code snippets for common analysis patterns.

**Store location**: `s3://us-west-2.opendata.source.coop/earthblox/cciwr/data/cciwr.zarr`

---

## Store structure

The store contains **three groups**, each a separate N-dimensional array dataset:

| Group | Dimensions | Description |
|-------|-----------|-------------|
| `RC` | `(ghm, gcm, ssp, horizon, season, lat, lon)` | Relative change (%) vs. 1985–2014 baseline |
| `FUTUR` | `(ghm, gcm, ssp, horizon, season, lat, lon)` | Absolute future value (mm) averaged over the 30-yr horizon |
| `HISTO` | `(ghm, gcm, season, lat, lon)` | Historical baseline (mm) averaged over 1985–2014 |

Each group holds **three hydrological variables**:

| Variable | ISIMIP source(s) | Physical quantity |
|----------|-----------------|-------------------|
| `qr` | `qr` + `qrd` (WaterGAP only) | Diffuse groundwater recharge |
| `qtot` | `qtot` | Total runoff |
| `evap_total` | `evap-total` | Actual evapotranspiration |

**Coordinate values**

| Dimension | Values |
|-----------|--------|
| `ghm` | `cwatm`, `jules-es-vn6p3`, `miroc-integ-land`, `watergap2-2e` |
| `gcm` | `gfdl-esm4`, `ipsl-cm6a-lr`, `mpi-esm1-2-hr`, `mri-esm2-0`, `ukesm1-0-ll` |
| `ssp` | `ssp126`, `ssp370`, `ssp585` |
| `horizon` | `2030`, `2055`, `2085` (centre of 30-yr window) |
| `season` | `yearly`, `DJF`, `MAM`, `JJA`, `SON` |
| `lat` | 89.75 → −89.75 (0.5° step, **descending**) |
| `lon` | −179.75 → 179.75 (0.5° step, ascending) |

**Storage layout** (Zarr v3, sharded) — RC / FUTUR:

| Level | Shape | Role |
|-------|-------|------|
| Inner chunk | `(4 ghm, 5 gcm, 1 ssp, 1 horizon, 1 season, 20 lat, 20 lon)` | Read granularity — a point/small-AOI read fetches only the inner chunk(s) it touches |
| Shard | `(4 ghm, 5 gcm, 1 ssp, 1 horizon, 1 season, 360 lat, 720 lon)` | Storage object — one shard holds the full global map for a single ssp/horizon/season |

Requires **Zarr v3** (`zarr>=3`) to read the sharded store.

---

## Quick-start: open the store

```python
import xarray as xr
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.colors as mcolors
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import cartopy.crs as ccrs
import cartopy.feature as cfeature

# ── Store location ──────────────────────────────────────────────
ZARR_PATH = 's3://us-west-2.opendata.source.coop/earthblox/cciwr/data/cciwr.zarr'

# ── Open all three groups (anonymous S3 access, lazy — no data loaded yet) ──
storage_options = {'anon': True}
ds_rc    = xr.open_zarr(ZARR_PATH, group='RC',    consolidated=True, storage_options=storage_options)
ds_futur = xr.open_zarr(ZARR_PATH, group='FUTUR', consolidated=True, storage_options=storage_options)
ds_histo = xr.open_zarr(ZARR_PATH, group='HISTO', consolidated=True, storage_options=storage_options)

ds_rc
```

---

## Case study 1 — Ensemble percentiles of groundwater recharge RC at a POI (Lyon)

Compute the **25th percentile, median, and 75th percentile** of the relative change in
groundwater recharge (`qr`) across all GHM × GCM combinations at a single point of interest,
for a user-defined SSP, horizon, and season.

The POI is snapped to the nearest 0.5° grid cell automatically.

```python
# ── User parameters ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
POI_LAT  = 45.75   # Lyon city centre (snapped to nearest 0.5° cell)
POI_LON  = 4.75
SSP      = 'ssp585'
HORIZON  = 2085
SEASON   = 'yearly'

# ── Select the nearest grid cell for the POI ────────────────────────────────
# lat is descending, so method='nearest' works correctly with sel()
poi_rc = ds_rc['qr'].sel(
    ssp=SSP,
    horizon=HORIZON,
    season=SEASON,
    lat=POI_LAT,
    lon=POI_LON,
)
# poi_rc shape: (ghm, gcm)  — all ensemble members at this cell

# Stack ghm × gcm into a flat ensemble dimension for quantile computation
ensemble = poi_rc.stack(member=('ghm', 'gcm'))

q10  = float(ensemble.quantile(0.10))
q25  = float(ensemble.quantile(0.25))
med  = float(ensemble.quantile(0.50))
q75  = float(ensemble.quantile(0.75))
q90  = float(ensemble.quantile(0.90))

snapped_lat, snapped_lon = float(poi_rc.lat), float(poi_rc.lon)

print(f'Scenario     : {SSP}, horizon {HORIZON}, season {SEASON}')
print(f'Variable     : qr (groundwater recharge, relative change %)')
print(f'  25th percentile : {100 * q25:+.1f} %')
print(f'  Median          : {100 * med:+.1f} %')
print(f'  75th percentile : {100 * q75:+.1f} %')
```

```python
# ── Percentile-box chart across all three horizons ───────────────────────────
# Reuses POI_LAT, POI_LON, SSP, SEASON from Case study 1 parameters.

VARIABLE = 'qr'          # variable to chart
HORIZONS       = [2030, 2055, 2085]
HORIZON_LABELS = ['2016–2045', '2041–2070', '2071–2100']

VAR_LABELS = {
    'qtot':       'Total Runoff',
    'qr':         'Groundwater Recharge',
    'evap_total': 'Actual Evapotranspiration',
}
SSP_LABELS = {
    'ssp126': 'SSP1 (RCP 2.6)',
    'ssp370': 'SSP3 (RCP 7.0)',
    'ssp585': 'SSP5 (RCP 8.5)',
}

# ── Collect percentiles for every horizon ────────────────────────────────────
horizon_stats = {}
snapped_lat_chart = snapped_lon_chart = None

for h in HORIZONS:
    # Exact match on string/categorical dims first; nearest-neighbour only for lat/lon
    poi_h = (
        ds_rc[VARIABLE]
        .sel(ssp=SSP, horizon=h, season=SEASON)
        .sel(lat=POI_LAT, lon=POI_LON, method='nearest')
    )
    ensemble_h = 100.0 * poi_h.stack(member=('ghm', 'gcm')).values

    if snapped_lat_chart is None:
        snapped_lat_chart = float(poi_h.lat)
        snapped_lon_chart = float(poi_h.lon)

    horizon_stats[h] = {
        'q10': float(np.nanpercentile(ensemble_h, 10)),
        'q25': float(np.nanpercentile(ensemble_h, 25)),
        'med': float(np.nanpercentile(ensemble_h, 50)),
        'q75': float(np.nanpercentile(ensemble_h, 75)),
        'q90': float(np.nanpercentile(ensemble_h, 90)),
        'n':   int(np.sum(~np.isnan(ensemble_h))),
    }

# ── Chart ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))

x     = np.arange(len(HORIZONS))
width = 0.55

COLOR_OUTER  = '#c8c8c8'   # 10th – 90th percentile band
COLOR_IQR    = '#787878'   # 25th – 75th IQR
COLOR_MEDIAN = '#303030'   # median line

for i, h in enumerate(HORIZONS):
    s = horizon_stats[h]

    # 10th – 90th band (lightest)
    ax.bar(i, s['q90'] - s['q10'], bottom=s['q10'],
           color=COLOR_OUTER, width=width, zorder=2, linewidth=0)

    # 25th – 75th IQR (medium)
    ax.bar(i, s['q75'] - s['q25'], bottom=s['q25'],
           color=COLOR_IQR, width=width, zorder=3, linewidth=0)

    # Median line
    ax.hlines(s['med'], i - width / 2, i + width / 2,
              colors=COLOR_MEDIAN, linewidths=2.5, zorder=4)

# Reference line at 0 %
ax.axhline(0, color='black', linewidth=0.9, zorder=1)

# Axes formatting
ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(HORIZON_LABELS, fontsize=11)
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f'{v:.0f}%'))
ax.set_ylabel(
    f'Relative change in\n{VAR_LABELS.get(VARIABLE, VARIABLE)} since 1985–2014 [%]',
    fontsize=10,
)
ax.tick_params(axis='y', labelsize=10)
ax.set_xlim(-0.55, len(HORIZONS) - 0.45)
ax.set_ylim(-100, 100)

# Major + minor horizontal grid
ax.yaxis.set_minor_locator(plt.MultipleLocator(5))
ax.yaxis.grid(True, which='major', linewidth=0.5, color='lightgrey', zorder=0)
ax.yaxis.grid(True, which='minor', linewidth=0.25, color='#e8e8e8', zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
ax.spines[['top', 'right']].set_visible(False)

# Title
ssp_label = SSP_LABELS.get(SSP, SSP)
n_members = horizon_stats[HORIZONS[0]]['n']
ax.set_title(
    f'Lat: {snapped_lat_chart}°, Lon: {snapped_lon_chart}° – '
    f'Seasonality: {SEASON.capitalize()} – {ssp_label}',
    fontsize=11, pad=10,
)

# Footer — ensemble size + legend explanation
ax.text(
    0.5, -0.10,
    f'Based on {n_members} ensemble members',
    ha='center', va='top', transform=ax.transAxes,
    fontstyle='italic', fontsize=9,
)
ax.text(
    0.5, -0.18,
    'Outer box: 10th–90th percentile  ·  Inner box: 25th–75th percentile  ·  Line: median',
    ha='center', va='top', transform=ax.transAxes,
    fontstyle='italic', fontsize=8, color='#555555',
)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Case study 2 — Map of ensemble-median RC in total runoff over Europe

Compute the **ensemble median** (across all GHM × GCM combinations) of the relative change in
total runoff (`qtot`) over Europe, for a user-defined SSP, horizon, and season.

The map uses a diverging blue–white–red colormap centred on 0% to make drying vs. wetting
signals immediately visible.

```python
# ── User parameters ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SSP     = 'ssp585'
HORIZON = 2085
SEASON  = 'yearly'

# Europe bounding box / Change by your area of interest.
LAT_MIN, LAT_MAX = 34.0, 72.0
LON_MIN, LON_MAX = -25.0, 45.0

# ── Spatial slice — lat is descending so min/max order is reversed ───────────
europe_rc = ds_rc['qtot'].sel(
    ssp=SSP,
    horizon=HORIZON,
    season=SEASON,
    lat=slice(LAT_MAX, LAT_MIN),   # descending axis
    lon=slice(LON_MIN, LON_MAX),
)
# europe_rc shape: (ghm, gcm, lat, lon)

# Ensemble median across all GHM × GCM pairs
median_rc = europe_rc.median(dim=['ghm', 'gcm']).compute()
# median_rc shape: (lat, lon)

# ── Diverging colormap centred on 0 ─────────────────────────────────────────
vmax = float(np.nanpercentile(np.abs(median_rc.values), 95))
norm = mcolors.TwoSlopeNorm(vmin=-vmax, vcenter=0, vmax=vmax)

# ── Map ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(
    figsize=(8, 7),
    subplot_kw={'projection': ccrs.PlateCarree()},
)
ax.set_extent([LON_MIN, LON_MAX, LAT_MIN, LAT_MAX], crs=ccrs.PlateCarree())

img = ax.pcolormesh(
    median_rc.lon.values,
    median_rc.lat.values,
    median_rc.values,
    norm=norm,
    cmap='RdBu',
    transform=ccrs.PlateCarree(),
)

# Overlay borders and coastlines
ax.add_feature(cfeature.BORDERS, linewidth=0.7, edgecolor='black')
ax.add_feature(cfeature.COASTLINE, linewidth=0.8)
ax.add_feature(cfeature.RIVERS, linewidth=0.4, edgecolor='steelblue', alpha=0.6)
ax.gridlines(draw_labels=False, linewidth=0.3, color='grey', alpha=0.5)

cbar = plt.colorbar(img, ax=ax, orientation='vertical', pad=0.02, fraction=0.03)
cbar.set_label('Relative change in total runoff', fontsize=10)
cbar.formatter = mticker.PercentFormatter(xmax=1.0, decimals=0)
cbar.update_ticks()

ax.set_title(
    f'Ensemble-median RC — qtot | {SSP}, horizon {HORIZON}, {SEASON}\n'
    f'(n = {len(ds_rc.ghm) * len(ds_rc.gcm)} ensemble members)',
    fontsize=11,
)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

![Ensemble-median relative change in total runoff over Europe](https://data.source.coop/earthblox/cciwr/docs/case_study_2_europe_median_runoff.png)

## Case study 3 — Model consensus on a drying threshold (groundwater recharge)

The ensemble median tells you the central signal, but not how *confident* the models are.
A more decision-relevant question is: **for a given level of stress, how many of the
ensemble members agree that it will be reached?**

Here we map **model consensus** over Europe — the percentage of the GHM × GCM members
that project a relative change in groundwater recharge (`qr`) **below a chosen drying
threshold**. The threshold is set with the `THRESHOLD` parameter at the top of the next cell
(default: **−20%**). A value of 100% means *every* model agrees the cell dries by at least
that much; 0% means *no* model does. Note that the number of available members can vary from
pixel to pixel, so the consensus is normalised by the valid members at each cell rather than
a fixed count. This turns the raw ensemble into a transparent, risk-oriented agreement map,
using a sequential colormap where darker = stronger consensus on drying.

```python
# ── User parameters ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SSP       = 'ssp585'
HORIZON   = 2085
SEASON    = 'yearly'    # could also do seasonal slices (e.g. 'DJF', 'MAM', 'JJA', 'SON') for a more seasonal perspective
VARIABLE  = 'qr'        # groundwater recharge
THRESHOLD = -0.20       # drying stress: count members with RC below -20%

# Europe bounding box (same extent as Case study 2).
LAT_MIN, LAT_MAX = 34.0, 72.0
LON_MIN, LON_MAX = -25.0, 45.0

# ── Spatial slice — lat is descending so min/max order is reversed ───────────
europe_rc = ds_rc[VARIABLE].sel(
    ssp=SSP,
    horizon=HORIZON,
    season=SEASON,
    lat=slice(LAT_MAX, LAT_MIN),   # descending axis
    lon=slice(LON_MIN, LON_MAX),
)
# europe_rc shape: (ghm, gcm, lat, lon)

# ── Model consensus: fraction of members with RC below the drying threshold ──
# Count members satisfying the stress, ignoring NaNs, then divide by valid count.
# The number of valid members varies from pixel to pixel (it is NOT always 20),
# so we normalise by the per-pixel valid count rather than a fixed denominator.
below     = (europe_rc < THRESHOLD)
n_below   = below.sum(dim=['ghm', 'gcm'])
n_valid   = europe_rc.notnull().sum(dim=['ghm', 'gcm'])
consensus = (n_below / n_valid).where(n_valid > 0).compute()   # 0–1, NaN where no data
# consensus shape: (lat, lon)

# ── Sequential colormap (0–100% agreement) ──────────────────────────────────
norm = mcolors.Normalize(vmin=0.0, vmax=1.0)

# ── Map ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(
    figsize=(8, 7),
    subplot_kw={'projection': ccrs.PlateCarree()},
)
ax.set_extent([LON_MIN, LON_MAX, LAT_MIN, LAT_MAX], crs=ccrs.PlateCarree())

img = ax.pcolormesh(
    consensus.lon.values,
    consensus.lat.values,
    consensus.values,
    norm=norm,
    cmap='YlOrRd',
    transform=ccrs.PlateCarree(),
)

# Overlay borders and coastlines
ax.add_feature(cfeature.BORDERS, linewidth=0.7, edgecolor='black')
ax.add_feature(cfeature.COASTLINE, linewidth=0.8)
ax.add_feature(cfeature.RIVERS, linewidth=0.4, edgecolor='steelblue', alpha=0.6)
ax.gridlines(draw_labels=False, linewidth=0.3, color='grey', alpha=0.5)

cbar = plt.colorbar(img, ax=ax, orientation='vertical', pad=0.02, fraction=0.03)
cbar.set_label(f'Model consensus on RC < {THRESHOLD:+.0%} (share of members)', fontsize=10)
cbar.formatter = mticker.PercentFormatter(xmax=1.0, decimals=0)
cbar.update_ticks()

ax.set_title(
    f'Model consensus on drying — {VAR_LABELS.get(VARIABLE, VARIABLE)} '
    f'RC < {THRESHOLD:+.0%}\n'
    f'{SSP}, horizon {HORIZON}, {SEASON}',
    fontsize=11,
)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

![Model consensus on drying of groundwater recharge over Europe](https://data.source.coop/earthblox/cciwr/docs/case_study_3_europe_consensus_drying.png)

## Resources & references

### Underlying source data — ISIMIP3b
This composite dataset is derived entirely from the **ISIMIP3b** (Inter-Sectoral Impact Model
Intercomparison Project, phase 3b) global water-sector simulation archive. Monthly time series
of total runoff (`qtot`), diffuse groundwater recharge (`qr` / `qrd`), and actual
evapotranspiration (`evap-total`) were downloaded from the ISIMIP data repository
([https://data.isimip.org/](https://data.isimip.org/)) under the `2015soc` experiment
([protocol](https://protocol.isimip.org/#/ISIMIP3b/water_global)). The historical reference
period uses the `historical_histsoc_default` specifier; future projections use the
`ssp126_2015soc-from-histsoc_default`, `ssp370_2015soc-from-histsoc_default`, and
`ssp585_2015soc-from-histsoc_default` specifiers for SSP1-2.6, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5
respectively. The full simulation data are cited as:

> Gosling, S. N., Müller Schmied, H., Bradley, A., Burek, P., Gedney, N., Grillakis, M.,
> Guillaumot, L., Hanasaki, N., Ito, A., Kou-Giesbrecht, S., Koutroulis, A., Nishina, K.,
> Otta, K., Sahu, R.-K., Satoh, Y., and Schewe, J. (2024).  
> *ISIMIP3b Simulation Data from the Global Water Sector (v1.3).*  
> ISIMIP Repository. DOI: [10.48364/ISIMIP.230418.3](https://doi.org/10.48364/ISIMIP.230418.3)
